messages:
anya: Quick check-in — after the dma-buf export/import path landed I hit a divergence where imported buffers sometimes show stale page refcounts when we tear down pinned-host-backing. Repro: run a tenant stress test that flips between export/import and local host-pinned reuse.

sam: ugh, seen similar. is this the one where the importer doesn't call the release callback in the fastpath?

anya: maybe. I captured a minimal trace:
```
trace: tenantA -> export(fd) -> import(fd) -> mmap -> munmap -> importer never calls dma_buf_put() in the async detach path
```

jorge: can you paste the diff of the new export path? my guess is ordering: we do an attach, then we hand a raw page pointer to the allocator, but the allocator's free path assumes it owns the pin and calls dma_buf_detach first. race on detach vs exporter unref could leave pages resident with >0 refcnt but inaccessible.

anya: attaching the logs: I see attach, mmap, allocator_free, dma_buf_detach, then exporter_put. but sometimes exporter_put arrives before the allocator_free completes due to work-queue reordering.

ellie: that sounds like a visibility/order problem across our worker threads. we probably need an explicit ownership transfer handshake instead of relying on refcounts alone. refcounts are racy across async teardown ordering.

sam: idea: introduce an allocator flag ALLOC_DMABUF_EXPLICIT_HANDOFF. when set, allocator_free will queue an ownership-release task and wait for a completion event (or mark transient state) before issuing dma_buf_detach. exporter_put must observe that state and call a complement API to finalize. keeps ordering deterministic.

jorge: i like the explicit handoff notion but be careful about blocking in free on hot paths. need a nonblocking protocol: state machine transitions (ACTIVE -> HANDOFF_PENDING -> RELEASED) and a fastpath that can steal ownership if the other side is in HANDOFF_PENDING for >X ms.

anya: agreed. how about: allocator_free sets HANDOFF_PENDING and emits an async completion token (opaque 64-bit). exporter_put must call handoff_complete(token) or the token times out and a compensating reclaim path runs. we can emit metrics: dma_handoff_wait_ms, handoff_timeouts, stolen_handoffs.

ellie: also need to address memory visibility: after handoff_complete we must ensure any writes to page metadata are published. add an smp_wmb() equivalent or use atomic ops for the state transition. otherwise importer may see RELEASING page metadata stale.

sam: good call. use atomic_exchange to move state, and pair with acquire/release semantics on the token handshake. that keeps kernel vs user-space ordering sane.

jorge: another angle: ensure dma-buf export path returns a signed export cookie that encodes the allocator version and a small nonce. importer validates cookie against current allocator ABI (so forward/backwards mismatches fail early).

anya: that will help debugging. I also want a debug-build option to assert that no exported fd is closed while HANDOFF_PENDING counters > 0. panic in dev.

ellie: API surface proposal (sketch):
- dma_buf_export_with_handoff(fd, flags) -> {cookie, token}
- allocator_handoff_claim(token) -> ok|retry
- allocator_handoff_complete(token) -> finalizes detach
- allocator_handoff_force(token) -> admin path to steal after timeout

sam: keep names short. also we need to document invariants: who may call handoff_claim (only importer or allocator?), whether token is single-use, and what happens on process crash. add kernel-level leak detector to scan HANDOFF_PENDING tokens older than 5m and emit a metric and optional reclamation.

anya: process-crash recovery is critical: if importer dies after import but before handoff_complete, pages could be pinned forever. force reclaim via netlink admin or evictor. evictor-bot: note: scheduling reclaim task for orphaned handoffs.

evictor-bot: auto-note: enqueued reclaim job for orphaned-handoff-scanner every 1h. telemetry labels: orphaned_handoffs, orphaned_handoff_age_max_ms.

jorge: minor perf thought: for hot small allocations used by model KV caches, the extra handshake may add latency. we should make ALLOC_DMABUF_HOT_ALLOWED that keeps the old refcounted fastpath but enables periodic validator that flips any leaking pins to handed-off after a threshold. i.e., hybrid mode.

ellie: test plan:
- unit tests for state transitions + token lifecycle
- end-to-end stress that toggles export/import under heavy mem churn
- fuzz: random delay between exporter_put and allocator_free
- integration: verify no pinned pages survive tenant shutdown (leak detector)

anya: ok. next steps: I'll open an RFC PR with the state-machine diagram, token encoding, and proposed kernel APIs. sam, can you prototype the user-space importer changes (handshake calls)? jorge, can you draft the evictor reclamation flow and metrics? ellie, please list memory visibility asserts and kernel atomic ordering notes for the RFC.

sam: on it. i'll add a small shim in the importer library and run the tenant stress harness.

jorge: will sketch the evictor reclamation with backoff and admin override.

ellie: I'll write the ordering notes and a checklist for kernel audits. also add pointer to a small litmus test we can run under tsan/lockdep.

anya: thanks all :thumbsup: let's aim to have the RFC PR up by EOD Friday so we can iterate before next week's sprint.

sam: quick question — do we want to expose handoff telemetry per-tenant or per-device? per-tenant probably better for billing and debugging.

anya: per-tenant + per-device labels. done.

ellie: one more: log format for reclaim events should include token, age_ms, originating_pid, tenant_id, and allocator_gen so postmortems are easier.

anya: noted. will include examples in the RFC.

jorge: ping me once the PR exists and i'll run the fuzz harness.

anya: will do. thanks everyone.
